newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares lower at open, focus on Omni.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares lower at open, focus on Omni.

text.p: Singapore shares were lower at the open on Wednesday with the focus mainly in newly-listed Omni Industries.

Dealers said the weaker market sentiment took the shine off Omni Industries. "The stock has potential to be higher but it is dampened by the wider market. There is interest to buy at below S$0.70," said one broker.

The electronics mould-making firm hit a high of S$0.785 before slipping to around S$0.73 after 50 minutes of trading. Volume was brisk with more than 19 million shares traded. The Straits Times Industrial Index was down 2.38 points to 2,187.06.
Total market volume was 52 million with 131 losers outpacing 42 gainers.
Computer maker IPC rose on news of it selling some shares in the company at a premium to a South Korean firm. IPC shares were up 1.5 Singapore cents to S$0.535 with over two million traded.
Dealers said Malaysian over-the-counter stocks remained weak with retail players getting out of their positions.
Blue chips, including Singapore Press foreign, UOB foreign and Keppel, were higher by between 10 to 20 Singapore cents in light volumes.
